note: THIS IS NOT KATE RYAN. No photograph of Kate Ryan was found. She stands in for her because she is an Irish woman photographed in Ireland in 1903, the year before the scene, and by appearance of about the same age as Kate Ryan in 1904 (54; born April 1850 in Ireland, 1900 census). The woman is not named and her age is not recorded: the age is a reading of the picture, not a fact from the record. She is a rural Achill Island woman at a spinning wheel, not a cook in a city house. The LC caption card's tracings include 'Husband & wife', which is all the record says about who the two sitters are. A stereograph of a thatched stone cottage on Achill Island, Co. Mayo: an older bearded man in a hat and waistcoat stands at left; a woman sits at a spinning wheel at right, facing the camera. Her face is frontal and evenly lit: hair parted in the centre and drawn back, a broad forehead with lines, deep-set eyes, a straight nose, a wide mouth, a firm chin; she wears a dark buttoned bodice with a pale apron over her lap. At about 175 px across the face is soft (a small stereo print scanned large) but the structure reads.
what_it_supplies: the proportions of an Irish countrywoman's face of about the right age, frontal, in the scene's own decade
the plain dark bodice and drawn-back hair of a working woman in 1903
what_it_does_not_supply: Kate Ryan's face, her age, her colouring, or anything about her
a cook's working dress or a city servant's appearance
the face's depth (one view only); fine skin detail (soft at this scale)
